central_model: Use a two-layer evidence graph: independent, atomic assertion records for individually supported facts, and context-rich Causal Workflow Units connected by typed causal relations. This adapts GO’s distinction between standard independent annotations and GO-CAM Activity Units.

architecture_principles.principle: Keep an atomic assertion as a separately addressable record, rather than conflating all findings from a report.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: GO states that each standard annotation is independent. Separate causal links, contrasts, and validation claims can therefore be revised or qualified without rewriting the whole study representation.

architecture_principles.principle: Require a minimal evidence-bearing tuple for each asserted link.
architecture_principles.source_locator: Standard GO annotations — “A standard GO annotation minimally contains”
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: The source requires an entity, controlled concept, reference, and evidence code. Analogously, every review assertion can retain its subject/object, typed relation, source locator, and evidence characterization.

architecture_principles.principle: Model the primary analytic unit with its enabling entity and operating context.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: An Activity Unit combines molecular activity, gene product, and context including location, biological program, cell type, and life-cycle stage. A causal workflow unit can similarly bind an analysis step or causal link to cohort, omics layer, tissue/cell context, time/age state, and study setting.

architecture_principles.principle: Connect contextualized units with explicit, semantically defined causal relation types.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: GO-CAM connects Activity Units through clearly defined Relations Ontology relations. Typed edges prevent a causal effect, association, participation relation, and location/context relation from being collapsed into one generic link.

architecture_principles.principle: Allow nested context rather than forcing one flat study label.
architecture_principles.source_locator: GO-Causal Activity Models — Biological Process context; GO-CAM data model
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: The source permits processes nested within broader processes. The review can nest contrasts or workflow stages within analyses, analyses within studies, and studies within reports while preserving their distinct identities.

architecture_principles.principle: Represent explicit negation and unresolved conflict as assertions, not as missing data.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: GO distinguishes experimentally supported NOT statements from negative/inconclusive results and permits positive and NOT statements together when literature conflicts. This supports explicit null/contradictory causal-link records with their own evidence, while leaving absence of evidence unasserted.

architecture_principles.principle: Treat the evidence base as open-world and versioned.
architecture_principles.source_locator: Standard GO annotation principles — Open-world assumption; GO as a dynamic source of biological knowledge
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Missing extraction must not mean a study or link is absent or false. Time-stamped curation and correction history preserve the distinction between unknown, not captured, superseded, and contradicted.

architecture_principles.principle: Enforce integrity rules at record level.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: GO requires valid identifiers, an evidence code and reference for every annotation, and excludes retracted publications. Equivalent validation makes review synthesis auditable and blocks unsupported or invalid causal assertions.

unit_and_boundary_rules: Report: a bibliographic source object; it may describe one or more studies and supplies citable source evidence.
Study: a distinct empirical investigation or cohort/experiment described by a report; do not equate it with the report.

Causal Workflow Unit: the contextualized unit of causal analysis, analogous to a GO-CAM Activity Unit; attach population/model, biological setting, omics inputs, intervention/exposure, outcome, assumptions, and analytic stage here.
Causal Link: one typed edge from a source unit to a target unit; retain direction and relation semantics separately from contextual membership or location.

Contrast: a comparison specification attached to the workflow/link it identifies; model it separately from the causal relation so alternative age, exposure, tissue, or intervention contrasts remain distinguishable.
Validation: an independent supporting, challenging, or replication assertion linked to the exact workflow or causal link it evaluates; do not merge it into the original evidence.
Source Evidence: an atomic provenance record attached to each asserted entity, relation, contrast, or validation claim; it includes a report reference and an evidence characterization.
Permit multiple workflow units and multiple causal links per study, and multiple evidence records per claim.
Do not infer a negative causal conclusion from absent records; reserve explicit negative records for evidence-grounded non-effects or incompatibility, with scope stated.
provenance_and_evidence_rules: Every extracted causal-link assertion must carry at least one source reference and an evidence-type field, following the minimum-content and quality-control concepts in “Standard GO annotations” and “Annotation Quality Control.”
Use controlled identifiers for reports, studies, entities, workflows, contrasts, and relation types; validate identifier integrity (Annotation Quality Control).

Store a precise within-source locator for each evidence record (for example, figure, table, supplement, methods section, or result statement); the supplied source establishes reference-bearing assertions, while this is the review-specific granularity needed for auditability.
Record curator/reviewer status or extraction mode separately from scientific evidence type, reflecting the source’s distinction between expert-reviewed and automated annotations.
Preserve conflicting evidence as coexisting, source-specific records; do not overwrite one with another (The NOT modifier).

Maintain curation timestamps/version history and permit corrections because the knowledge base is a “living document”/dynamic source (Standard GO annotation principles; GO as a dynamic source of biological knowledge).
Reject or flag evidence from retracted reports and require minimum provenance before a record is synthesis-eligible (Annotation Quality Control).

adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.source_basis: GO-CAM data model — Activity Unit plus contextual biological program, location, cell type, and life-cycle stage
adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.use_in_review: Represent a particular causal-analysis workflow in a study, including multi-omics measurements, causal method, biological context, and target estimand.

adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.source_basis: GO-CAM data model — Activity Units connected by clearly defined causal relations
adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.use_in_review: Encode direction, sign/effect qualifier where justified, mechanism/status, and the exact workflow units connected; avoid generic “related to” edges.

adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.source_basis: Standard GO annotations — independent statements with gene product, term, reference, and evidence code
adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.use_in_review: Attach independently citable evidence to each causal relation, contrast definition, and validation result.

adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.source_basis: Standard GO annotations — annotation extensions; GO-CAM biological context
adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.use_in_review: Add tissue, cell type, age/life stage, assay, molecular layer, exposure, and other contextual qualifiers without duplicating the core causal link.
Represent a supported null, incompatibility, or challenged mechanism as a scoped assertion rather than deleting positive evidence or treating missing extraction as negative evidence.
Require valid identifiers, source evidence, evidence classification, and retraction screening before synthesis or visualization.

cautions: The source’s causal model concerns biological activities, not statistical causal identification; any adaptation must separately encode study design, estimand, assumptions, and identification method.
The source’s three GO aspects are not a sufficient schema for multi-omics studies; use them only as inspiration for separating activity/process/location context.
“NOT” in the source requires affirmative supporting evidence and is not a label for inconclusive or absent findings; apply the same discipline to null or negative causal claims.

Ontology propagation is only safe when relation semantics and hierarchy justify it. Do not automatically propagate causal findings across broader or narrower ages, tissues, exposures, omics layers, or outcomes.
GO’s open-world assumption means database absence is not evidence of biological absence; likewise, no extracted review record must not be interpreted as no study, no causal link, or no validation.
